newsitem.title: UK: Hardy boosted by Timor Sea breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: Hardy boosted by Timor Sea breakthrough.

text.p: Shares in Hardy Oil & Gas Plc rose 8-1/2 pence to 293 following overnight news that partners in the Bayu-Undan gas project had reached a basic agreement on how to develop the giant field in the Timor Sea, dealers said.
The participants selected BHP Petroleum to be the sole operator of the project, which is split between two joint venture groups.
The agreement signified a major step in developing Bayu Undan, which is estimated to have proven and probable reserves of 3.1 trillion cubic feet, said Hardy.
"The rapid development of this valuable asset shows every prospect of underpinning the steady growth of Hardy's activities in Australia," said John Walmsley, chief executive of Hardy.
The Bayu-Undan interest is one of Hardy's main assets.
The British oil exploration and production firm has a 15 percent interest in the joint venture led by Phillips Petroleum Co. BHP leads the other group.
